analysis.title: AI Debt Contagion: Credit Correlations Hit Highest Since The Iran War As Goldman Names The New "Defensives"
key_insights: Goldman's Global Credit Trader says price action since mid-October shows a threshold beyond which AI-related cost-of-capital concerns can threaten the broader growth narrative. The overhang has spread to non-AI credit, with spreads decompressing (lower-rated cohorts underperforming) and correlations moving higher.
Pairwise correlations of USD credit spread changes hit their highest level since the 1Q2026 Iran escalation. Across IG and HY, AI and non-AI lines have converged at the top.

Goldman's credit bear case was last weekend described as not bearish enough, with spreads expected to 'moderately overshoot' the March peaks of 93bp (IG) and 335bp (HY). With IG at 86bp and HY at 312bp five days later, whether the macro backdrop can support non-AI credit is now 'a qualified yes'.

Goldman's baseline is that growth is 'good enough' for higher-quality credit, with year-end forecasts of IG at 82bp and HY at 295bp. Lynam says valuations are tight by historical standards, the left tail is thicker, and broad-based dip buying is not prudent.

IG positioning: Goldman stays with its call from two weeks earlier, downgrading AA in favor of BBB. The AA end of IG is where the hyperscalers sit and where AI supply is coming from. The recent decompression in non-AI IG is seen as a chance for the spread ratio to compress again.

Microsoft, which had not sold a dollar bond since 2017, launched a 10-part dollar bond offering seeking at least $25 billion on the day of the note. Its CFO had said the night before that the company had not 'yet' tapped the debt market.

HY is split into three parts: AI-related, regular-way performing HY, and distressed. AI-related HY is neutral, particularly project finance structures, which are underwriting-dependent but keep an attractive yield. Banks are reported stuck holding a $15 billion bridge loan for Anthropic's Texas data center after a planned $5-7 billion junk bond takeout was shelved.

BBs are neutral because Goldman expects them to continue to absorb the brunt of AI-related financing, plus potential duration headwinds if rates drift higher. Single-Bs are overweight for carry, though dispersion within single-Bs is expected to rise. CCCs are underweight on macro and refinancing stress.

CCC performance: USD CCC bonds are down 5.3% YTD with spreads 422bp wider at 1,307bp and an all-in yield of 18%. CCC leveraged loans are down 9% YTD with spreads 845bp wider at 2,409bp, yielding 30%. BBs and single-Bs remain positive YTD.

Fallen-angel pipeline: $38 billion of USD downgrades to junk so far this year against a full-year forecast of $60 billion, leaving about $22 billion still to come. All of it is expected to land in the BB bucket.

For crossover investors, Goldman prefers moving down the capital structure over moving down in credit quality. Corporate hybrids 'offer compelling value' after the recent widening, and subordinated debt of money center banks also screens attractive.

New 'defensives' are defined by low correlation to AI spreads. In IG, Utilities, Financials and Healthcare/Pharma show lower correlation, and Energy also stands out in HY. Non-AI TMT trades closely with the AI trade. Every sector's correlation to AI spreads has risen in the past two weeks, with the HY index at its highest since July.

JPMorgan's Market Intelligence desk is less alarmed: credit markets are becoming more discriminating on AI infrastructure but nothing suggests a broader funding crisis. JPM estimates AI infrastructure has absorbed more than $500 billion of debt YTD, and credit analyst Erica Spear said growing supply may pressure spreads into 2027.

Fund performance: the 20 largest USD IG funds and ETFs hold $345 billion (five active), returning -0.5% YTD and +1.5% over the past month, driven largely by the rate rally since October 5. The 20 largest HY funds hold $202 billion (eleven active), returning +0.6% over one month, -0.9% over three months and +0.2% YTD, with less benefit from duration.

Active managers lagged: active IG funds trailed their benchmark by 0.7% in the past month, taking YTD excess return to -0.2%. Active HY managers lagged by 0.6% in the month and are ahead YTD by +0.9% only because of carry from higher all-in yields.

Europe: EUR credit has benefited from a lack of AI issuance, but elevated energy prices and sovereign and fiscal risks pushed spreads wider. Goldman prefers USD over EUR credit. EUR senior bank spreads have widened relative to non-financials even excluding France, and Goldman remains underweight French banks amid an expected Moody's downgrade of France.

Hedging: Goldman says macro index hedges (CDX, iTraxx) still work because stress in AI funding would hit growth broadly and credit spreads would move together. Protection costs more, with 3M implied vol near post-COVID medians in USD credit and at the 65th percentile in EUR. Skew has flattened and term structure is flatter, which improves the economics of payers and longer-dated hedges. Goldman advises using local rallies to add protection.
Rates strategists at Goldman note the past few weeks catalyzed a duration rally, with Treasuries acting as a hedge amid risk-off tone.
The article author notes Alphabet shed about half a trillion dollars in market cap on Wednesday and credit spreads widened again on the Friday of publication.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's macro baseline of 'good enough' growth supports higher-quality credit, with year-end forecasts of IG at 82bp and HY at 295bp. JPM sees credit becoming more discriminating but no broader funding crisis.
tension_points.bear_case: Valuations are tight, the left tail is thicker, and correlations to AI spreads have risen across sectors. JPM's Spear says supply may pressure spreads into 2027. Goldman does not view broad dip buying as prudent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further rise in sector correlation to AI spreads or a failure of AI financing takeouts, such as the shelved Anthropic junk bond, would undercut the 'qualified yes' on non-AI credit.
